piezas.titular: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, for now only for cybersecurity specialists
piezas.entradilla: Google DeepMind has announced its new frontier model, which for now is used only by a small group of cyber-defence professionals. There is no date for the general public.
cuerpo: On 28 October 2026 Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which it describes as its most capable model to date and the successor to Gemini 4 Argon, released two weeks earlier. According to the company, it begins to become available this week to a subset of people working in cybersecurity defence and will gradually be extended to more trusted partners through the Fairwind programme.

Access for developers, businesses and the general public will come “as soon as possible”, according to Google, but [the announcement](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/) gives no date. For teachers, then, this is for now news about what is to come, not a tool that can be used in the classroom. That was precisely what was pointed out in the group: for the moment it is only an announcement.

Google attributes to the model improvements in programming, multi-step tasks and web development, with its biggest advance in cybersecurity. Among the figures it offers are first place in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 (59 points) and more than double the success rate of Argon in secure code generation. These are results published by the company itself, with no independent verification in what was consulted.

API pricing, once it is generally available, will be $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens during an introductory period, and $4 and $20 afterwards. The announcement makes no mention of educational uses.
piezas.comprobado: Leído el anuncio oficial en blog.google: fecha 28-10-2026, acceso inicial restringido a un subconjunto de defensores en ciberseguridad, ampliación gradual por el programa Fairwind, Argon lanzado “hace dos semanas”, cifras de benchmarks (índice v5.0, 59 puntos; más del doble de éxito en código seguro) y precios introductorio y posterior. Las cifras son autodeclaradas por Google. El enlace de X del grupo no se pudo abrir.
piezas.ilustracion: Esquema de escalera de acceso en tres peldaños: 'Ahora: defensa en ciberseguridad', 'Después: socios de confianza (Fairwind)', 'Más adelante, sin fecha: desarrolladoras, empresas y público', con el tercero en trazo discontinuo y un candado abierto a medias.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A staircase of three steps rising from left to right: the first, with a few people, is cybersecurity defence; the second, with more people, is trusted partners; the third, dashed and with a half-open padlock, is marked “no date”.

piezas.titular: Plec generates foldable Catalan dictations, with audio, so that students can mark their own work
piezas.entradilla: An open app creates lists of words or pseudowords to dictate in class, printed on a folded sheet so that students can check their own answers.
cuerpo: [Plec](https://plec.ortogra.fi/ca/), created by Aarón Fortuño according to the project’s website, is an open resource (MIT licence) for practising Catalan spelling. Teachers choose between dictations of words or of pseudowords, from 8 to 24 items, with an indicative level (middle primary, upper primary or secondary school) and filters by spelling difficulty. Its presentation mentions a catalogue of around 3,300 words.

The result is printed as a PDF with a fold into thirds or quarters of a sheet, so that the solution stays hidden: the teacher dictates, the students write and then unfold the sheet to mark their own work. Each dictation has a code that makes it possible to retrieve the same list, with the same words in the same order, from another device.

The words can be listened to, which allows it to be used as an independent task in class or at home. There is audio in Central Catalan and Valencian; the Mallorcan variety is on hold while its phonetic transcription is reviewed.
The app requires no accounts and does not store dictations on a server. It is entirely in Catalan.
piezas.comprobado: Abierta la web de la aplicación (plec.ortogra.fi/ca): autoría (Aarón Fortuño), opciones de 8 a 24 palabras, niveles, plegado en tercios o cuarto, código para recuperar la lista, audio central y valenciano con mallorquín en pausa, sin cuentas ni almacenamiento en servidor, licencia MIT, sitio en catalán. La cifra de unas 3.300 palabras procede de la presentación de la aplicación en el grupo; la web no da el total.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Diagram of three moments: “Dictated”, with a loudspeaker; “Written”, with a folded sheet on which students note their answers with the solution hidden; and “Marked”, with the sheet unfolded, the answers beside the solution and tick and cross marks.

piezas.titular: A prompt for creating interactive 3D lessons inspired by “Every Joule”
piezas.entradilla: A member of the groups shared a long prompt for an AI to generate an interactive 3D lesson in the style of a physics book about energy.
cuerpo: “Every Joule” is an interactive 3D book about energy published on [iamtechartist.com](https://iamtechartist.com/every-joule/). According to its page, it brings together ten GCSE and IGCSE physics lessons, in which learners predict, test and check the answer by lifting a flap, and earn a stamp on completing it. It includes notes for teachers and requires graphics acceleration in the browser. The website gives no individual author or licence.

To reproduce that style with other topics, a prompt in English was shared that asks a model for a single HTML file using Three.js. It demands the book metaphor, the predict–observe–test–explain–stamp flow, a side flap with a formula or code, and an interface in Spanish. It has a gap, “[TOPIC HERE]”, where the subject goes, for example photosynthesis or Newton’s laws.

Whoever shared it proposed trying it with Claude and other paid models and publishing the results. No results had yet been published in the day’s messages. As with any resource generated with AI, it is worth checking the scientific content and accessibility before taking it into the classroom.
piezas.comprobado: Abierta la página de Every Joule: diez lecciones, GCSE/IGCSE, secuencia predecir-probar-solapa-sello, notas docentes, requisito de aceleración gráfica, sin autoría ni licencia. No se ejecutó el prompt ni se comprobó que produzca resultados equivalentes; solo se describe su contenido tal como se compartió.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Diagram of three steps: “Prompt”, a sheet with a dashed gap for the topic; “3D book”, an open book with a lifted flap revealing the answer; and “Stamp”, with a tick mark on completing the lesson.

breves.texto: On 27 October the AEPD (Spain’s data protection authority) published a ten-point guide for people who use AI assistants and agents. It recommends that the agent prepares and the person approves, with minimal permissions and confirmation before sending, sharing or paying.
GitHub’s documentation states that teachers verified on GitHub Education can access Copilot Pro for free, and that eligibility is reassessed every month.

descartado: Recorte del uso gratuito de OpenCode (consulta de un miembro): no confirmado en fuentes oficiales; solo hay informes dispersos y no se encontró anuncio de recorte.
Vídeo de YouTube sobre Claude “reinventándose”: no se pudo saber de qué trata; sin fuente verificable.
Ampliación del bot de los grupos y /misrecursos: administración interna, excluida.
Laboratori de formulació y Reactius i sobrants (Felip Sarroca): publicados el 27 de octubre, no son noticia del 28.
Enlace a un tuit de la AEPD (28 de octubre): no se pudo abrir; se cubre el decálogo en un breve a partir de la fuente oficial.
Mensajes sobre límites de uso o reseteo y charla trivial: quejas personales o sin contenido.
repaso: Gemini 4 Carbon: reescrito el campo “comprobado” a lo realmente verificado en el anuncio de Google (se citaba un contraste con Android Authority que no se pudo repetir). El cuerpo era correcto.
Plec: titular sin la expresión confusa “modelo oculto”.
Plec: eliminado el alias de Telegram “xosqox” (identificación deducida); la autoría se da solo como figura en la web.
Plec: quitadas las cifras exactas “3.299 palabras y 96 pseudopalabras” (la web no las da; queda “cerca de 3.300” atribuido a la presentación).
Plec: quitados el plan de ampliar al castellano, la petición de voces y los “niveles como propuesta editorial”, que no constan en la fuente pública; quitado “gratuito” (la web dice abierto).
Every Joule: quitada la descripción de “dibujos de tinta” y “color como flujo de energía”, que la página no confirma (venía del prompt, no de la fuente); añadido el requisito de aceleración gráfica.
Breve de GitHub Education: quitado “correo institucional y documentos”, que esa página no dice.
